session-persistence-full-coverage.title: Report creation: full session persistence
session-persistence-full-coverage.description: Session state is now saved end-to-end — including when you load an existing JSON file instead of running a new corpus job. Clinical and biomaterial JSON file references are written to the Drive manifest the moment they are loaded, so the resume flow knows exactly which files to re-download. All text inputs in Section 2 (study matching), biomaterial template confirm, Section 3, and Section 1 are debounced and persisted in real time as you type. When you resume a session, matched studies are rebuilt from the stored clinical JSON with your per-study overrides (template selection, notes) re-applied automatically. Biomaterial files are similarly re-hydrated with their metaStepId and note overrides. Section 3 and Section 1 text inputs are restored the moment the GSheet data loads — no manual re-entry needed.

report-creation-sessions.title: Report creation: Drive-backed session resume
report-creation-sessions.description: The CTD 2.7.2 report-creation wizard saves a session manifest in your project's report_creation_corpus folder on Google Drive. Corpus and summary jobs are linked to that session so you can close the page, reopen later, and pick up from the last step — or resume an older incomplete session from the session name screen.

claimValidation.splitHelp: Split long PDFs into smaller chunks before extraction. Each chunk is sent to Gemini separately and results are merged.
claimValidation.splitReco0: Best for well-structured documents (slide decks, tables, numbered lists) where claims rarely run across page breaks.
claimValidation.splitReco1: Minimal safety net — catches claims split across exactly one page turn. Good for most structured reports.
claimValidation.splitRecoShortChunks: Short chunks already limit the area a claim can span; 1–2 pages overlap is usually enough here.
claimValidation.splitRecoLow: Good default. Catches most cross-boundary claims with minimal extra cost.
claimValidation.splitRecoMid: Solid choice for dense documents (research papers, legal contracts, technical specs) where multi-page arguments are common.
claimValidation.splitRecoHigh: High overlap — suitable for very dense prose (books, lengthy contracts). Expect noticeably longer processing.
claimValidation.splitRecoVeryHigh: Very high overlap. Processing time grows substantially; consider increasing the chunk size instead.
claimValidation.splitRecoTip: Tip: overlap above 25% rarely improves recall. Try increasing pages per chunk to {pages} to get the same coverage at lower cost.
claimValidation.accuracyTradeoffP1: Overlap pages are sent to the model twice — once in their original chunk and again at the start of the next. The model may extract the same claim multiple times, which the system deduplicates automatically.
claimValidation.accuracyTradeoffP2: However, deduplication is text-based: paraphrased or partially repeated claims may slip through, inflating the claim count and reducing overall precision. The higher the overlap, the greater this risk.
claimValidation.splitErrPagesMin: Pages per chunk must be at least 1.
claimValidation.splitErrOverlapTooBig: Overlap pages must be less than pages per chunk.

help.title: Agent nodes — quick guide
help.subtitle: Shortcuts and how the graph works
help.liToolbar1: Run all — Runs every agent step in dependency order (follow the arrows). Use Stop to cancel a run in progress.
help.liToolbar2: Reset layout — Rebuilds the graph from the agent and drops local-only changes: custom positions, nodes you added here, and rewired edges (after you confirm).
help.liCanvas1: Pan & zoom — Drag the background to pan; use the corner controls or trackpad / wheel zoom (React Flow defaults).
help.liCanvas2: New step on empty canvas — ⌘ or Ctrl + click the background: opens the same Add step menu as dragging from a handle. Choose Classic step to place a standalone node (Audit step is shown but not available yet).
help.liCanvas3: New step from a handle — Drag from a node’s handle to empty space: a menu opens; pick Classic step to add and wire the step (Audit step is not available yet).
help.liCanvas4: Connect steps — Drag from one handle to another node’s handle to add a dependency arrow (output → input).
help.liCanvas5: Click an edge — Opens a menu: fork a new branch, insert a step between the two endpoints, or pick a step type (where available).
help.liCanvas6: Drag edge endpoints — Reattach a wire to another handle. If you drop on an invalid target, the edge can be removed.
help.liNodes1: Click — Open the step (notes popup for local-only nodes; native step editor for steps that exist on the agent).
help.liNodes2: Double-click — Same as opening the step in the workflow editor.
help.liNodes3: Right-click or ⌘ / Ctrl + click — Context menu: edit or delete the node.
help.liNodes4: Enter — With a node selected, opens it (same as a single click).
help.liNodes5: Backspace / Delete — Removes selected nodes or edges.
help.liNodes6: Hover a node — Highlights upstream steps and incoming edges so you can read the dependency path at a glance (hidden while a run is animating).
help.liRun1: Steps show running, completed, failed, and queued states on the graph. Edges along the active path are animated.
help.liPersist1: Layout and edges for this agent are saved automatically in the browser (per project). Saving step content to the server still uses Save inside the step editor when you change configuration there.
help.liPersist2: Esc — Closes this guide, context menus, and the step-type picker when they are open.

tutorial.title: How agent nodes work
tutorial.subtitle: Short tour of the editable workflow graph
tutorial.step1Subtitle: Same agents as Canvas 272, with an editable graph
tutorial.step1Body:
**What you are looking at**
- **Agent nodes** shows your workflow as a graph: each box is a step and arrows show what runs before what.
- Unlike the read-only Canvas 272 view, **you can edit** the graph here: add steps, reconnect wires, and move nodes. Layout and wiring are saved automatically in your browser for this project.
- The **?agent=** URL selects which agent is open. Opening **Agent nodes** from the menu without that query always returns you to the agent list.
tutorial.step2Title: Pick an agent, open a step
tutorial.step2Body:
**Navigation**
- Use the **left column** to choose an agent. Collapse it to focus on the canvas; use the edge handle to bring the list back.
- **Single-click** a node to open the step (a notes popup for local-only nodes, or the full step editor in a frame for layers that exist on the agent).
- **Double-click** opens the step in the **workflow editor** when that path is available.
tutorial.step3Body:
**Execution and output**
- **Run all** walks every step in dependency order and may call models; use **Stop** to cancel. You may be asked to confirm first.
- **Simulate** animates flow on the graph without writing model output; you can pause, resume, or capture a GIF where that option exists.
- **Export doc** opens the structured document flow (review, section order, preview)—similar to Canvas 272 reporting.
tutorial.step4Body:
**Editing**
- **Pan and zoom** by dragging the background; use corner controls or trackpad / wheel zoom as usual.
- Add a step with **⌘ or Ctrl + click** on empty canvas, or drag from a node handle and pick **Classic step**.
- **Connect** steps by dragging from one handle to another (output → input). **Click an edge** for branch or insert-between actions when the menu offers them.
tutorial.step5Subtitle: Use the aurora ball to speak graph changes
tutorial.step5Body:
**Voice on this page**
- Click the **aurora ball** (left of the ALMA logo) to open voice, then speak while an agent is open here.
- **Insert between two steps:** for example say you want to insert a step between two connected nodes — a new node is placed on that edge.
- **Rewire:** for example ask to connect one step to another, or describe several links to add or remove for more complex rewiring.
- You can also say **add a step** or **remove connection**; changes apply to the graph you see here (same as manual edits).

document-quality.name: Document quality
document-quality.about: Infers what the document is for, then checks clarity, consistency, and proportionate issues — not a fixed regulatory checklist.

clarity-readability.name: Clarity & readability
clarity-readability.about: Jargon without context, vague qualifiers, buried leads, ambiguous references, and sentences that are hard to parse on first read.

consistency-style.name: Terminology & consistency
consistency-style.about: Same concept named different ways, abbreviation drift, list parallelism, tense/voice shifts, and heading vs body alignment.

clinical.name: Clinical Reviewer
clinical.about: Checks clinical study interpretation, endpoints, AEs, statistical claims, and GRADE alignment.

medical-writer.name: Medical Writer

fda-drugs.about: Checks US human drug / biologic submission-style content: IND/NDA/BLA expectations, labeling consistency, safety reporting, and pivotal study adequacy where claimed.

ema-drugs.anchor: Directive 2001/83/EC · Regulation (EC) No 726/2004 · SmPC / EPAR conventions

session.s0Body: You are naming this drafting session. That label is reused in filenames and agent names so your outputs stay easy to find later.
session.s1Body: Type a short, recognizable name in the input. It is a simple text field—nothing fancy: pick something your team will understand when they see exports or Drive folders.
session.s2Body: When you are ready, use Continue to enter the workflow. You can still adjust corpus and steps in the next screens; this just unlocks the rest of the wizard.

processing.s0Body: This screen shows background jobs—corpus creation, summaries, or hand-offs between stages. There is no separate menu here: status and progress are the main feedback.
processing.s1Body: Watch the progress bar and short status text. If something fails, the UI will usually surface an error and often a way to go back or retry.
processing.s2Body: Avoid closing the modal while a job runs unless you mean to cancel your session. If the screen seems stuck, wait a bit, then use any Back or recovery action the UI offers.

done.s0Body: Processing finished for this part of the pipeline. The wizard will move you toward study matching, or show loading while it prepares templates.
done.s1Body: If you see a spinner, templates are still loading. Otherwise you will continue to the table where studies are matched—use the main action on that screen when it appears.

matching.s0Body: Each row is one study document from your corpus summaries. The table is the main workspace: scroll to review every row before you continue.
matching.s1Body: Use the checkboxes to decide which studies become steps in the generated workflow. The header checkbox is a quick way to select or clear all visible rows.
matching.s2Body: The Instruction cell is usually a dropdown fed from your Google Sheet templates. Pick the prompt row that best fits each study—you can refine details later in preview or later sections.
matching.s3Body: Keywords are there for context; expand the Keywords row if you need a reminder. "Your input" is optional per-row notes. Use Back or Continue at the bottom when you are satisfied.

matchingPreview.s0Body: You are looking at a draft of the workflow: one card per step. Scan the list top to bottom—that order is how the agent will run.
matchingPreview.s1Body: Each card has a step title you can edit, a model dropdown to choose the LLM, and a User Input area for extra context. These are standard form controls: click, type, or pick from the list.
matchingPreview.s2Body: User instruction usually comes from your template; open the collapsible section if you need to tweak wording. When finished reviewing, use the actions at the bottom of the wizard to move on.

metaprocessing.s0Body: The app is indexing or summarizing your biomaterial corpus. Like the clinical processing screen, you mainly wait for status text and any progress shown here.
metaprocessing.s1Title: If you need to step back
metaprocessing.s1Body: Back returns you to the biomaterial corpus UI. Only use it if you really need to change files or settings; otherwise let the job finish.

sec3confirm.s0Body: This table lists drafting steps for Section 3 from your templates. Checkboxes control which rows are included when the agent is generated.
sec3confirm.s1Body: Each row shows a step name and a text area for optional notes. The pattern matches other wizard tables: select what you need, add context where it helps.
sec3confirm.s2Body: Use Back to return to an earlier step if you need to fix corpora or matching. Continue moves forward once required fields and selections look right.

sec1confirm.s0Body: Same idea as Section 3: rows come from your template sheet, with checkboxes to include or skip steps in the final agent.
sec1confirm.s1Body: Step numbers reflect how layers will be ordered after your clinical and Section 3 steps. Use "Your input" for brief notes saved on each layer.
sec1confirm.s2Body: Back and Continue behave like the rest of the wizard—no hidden menus. If a button is disabled, the tooltip or label usually says what is still missing.

generating.s0Body: The server is assembling layers, instructions, and bibliography from everything you confirmed. This view is intentionally minimal: spinner plus a short message.
generating.s1Body: Do not close the window until generation completes or shows an error. Large agents can take a minute; interrupting may leave the session in an inconsistent state.

metaConfirm.s1Body: Each row is one PDF from your biomaterial corpus (from the summary JSON). Here you confirm how many agent steps to create, which instruction template applies per file, and optional notes—before Section 3.
metaConfirm.s2Body: Use the header checkbox to select or clear all PDFs. Each row checkbox includes or excludes that PDF when you generate the agent. Unchecked rows are left out of the biomaterial layers.
metaConfirm.s3Body: The number is the order of biomaterial steps in the generated workflow (after your Section 2 clinical steps).
metaConfirm.s4Body: The PDF filename from your corpus / summary. One row per document that was indexed into the biomaterial corpus.
metaConfirm.s5Body: Choose a prompt row from the sect1MetaSteps tab in your templates Google Sheet. That instruction is used for this PDF's meta-section layer. When you opened this screen, each row was defaulted using KEY_WORD matching on the filename (or the first sheet row if needed).
metaConfirm.s6Body: Keywords come from the biomaterial summary JSON. Open the Keywords row to see tags; they help you verify the file and matching context.
metaConfirm.s7Body: Optional extra context for this step. It is saved as User Input on the layer when the agent is generated (same idea as Section 2).

ALMA includes a Voice Assistant that lets you control the app and create projects using your voice.

• Your voice input is sent to ALMA’s services to understand your requests and carry out actions (e.g. create a project, open a page).

By accepting, you agree to use the Voice Assistant in line with our Privacy and Terms of Use.

help.title: How skills work
help.lead: A skill is a reusable instruction you write once and attach to an agent. Once attached, it layers on top of every step the agent runs — like a standing rule the agent always follows.
help.appliesTitle: A skill applies to every step
help.appliesBody: Unlike an instruction inside a single step, a skill sits above the whole agent. Attach it once and it shapes the behaviour of Step 1, Step 2, and every step after — no need to repeat yourself.
help.how1Body: Click + and type the instruction, or import it from a file or Google Doc.
help.how2Body: Pick it from your library. It appears as a chip on the skills bar.
help.how3Body: The agent now follows the skill on every step, automatically.
help.ex1Body: Always respond in a professional, formal tone. Avoid slang and contractions.
help.ex2Body: Whenever you make a factual claim, cite the source it came from.
help.ex3Body: Return every answer as valid JSON with keys: summary, details, confidence.
help.faq1Q: How is a skill different from a step instruction?
help.faq1A: A step instruction only affects that one step. A skill applies on top of every step of the agent, so it's the right place for global rules like tone, format, or constraints.
help.faq2Q: Can I attach more than one skill?
help.faq2A: Yes. Attach as many as you need — they stack, and all attached skills apply together to every step.
help.faq3Q: Are skills shared across my agents?
help.faq3A: Skills live in your library and can be attached to any agent. Editing a skill updates it everywhere it's attached; removing it from one agent doesn't delete it from the library.
help.faq4A: Write one directly, or import from a PDF, DOCX, TXT, MD file, or a Google Doc — the text becomes the skill's instruction.
help.faq5Q: How do I remove a skill from an agent?
help.faq5A: Click the ✕ on the skill's chip in the skills bar. That detaches it from this agent but keeps it in your library.
